thread:
sara: heads up — production spike on text-gen-prod-1, 6x 5xxs since 10:14 UTC. KV prefix cache hit-rate dropped 91% -> 12% immediately after the kernel-selection rollout. paging @mike @chris

infra-bot: alert: metric=prefix_cache_miss_rate service=prefix-cache-prod value=0.88 threshold=0.2 window=2m

mike: digging in. quick scan shows the new kernel path toggled tokenizer_normalize_whitespace=true in the runtime flags for the rollout group. that changes key chefing for prefix cache (we canonicalize input before hashing).

chris: confirmed on cache-proxy logs — keys arriving from runtime look different: e.g. old key: "prefix:Hello, world!" new key: "prefix:hello, world!" (we lowercased / trimmed). hit logs -> \"miss\" repeated. also seeing thundering herd to origin: backend qps 4x.

sara: oh — kernel selection shouldn't have touched normalization. was that incidental side-effect of the faster tokenizer kernel? @mike do we have a quick rollback?

mike: there was a micro-optimization merged in the kernel branch: normalize -> small unicode fold + trim. it went through perf benchmarks but didn't run through cache-keying tests. rolling back now.

chris: meanwhile cache nodes are overloaded due to hot misses. suggestion: disable prefetch for the rollout shard to stop origin thrash and add a temporary rate-limit on miss fanout. roll call on commands?

dave: +1 to disabling prefetch. we have an ops runbook command: 
```
# disable prefetch for model rollout group
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://ops-api.internal/v1/cache/config -d '{"model_tag":"text-gen-v2-rollout","prefetch_enabled":false}'
```

emma: doing that now. also increasing cache node pool from 3 -> 6 while we stabilize (autoscaler will handle CPU, but we need immediate capacity).

infra-bot: action: config-change applied model_tag=text-gen-v2-rollout prefetch_enabled=false by emma at 10:22:03 UTC

mike: rollback of kernel flag started (canary -> off). estimate 2–3 minutes to propagate.

chris: origin qps back down 0.6x after prefetch disable and node bump. miss-rate slowly trending down. still seeing some clients with non-normalized keys (older SDKs).

sara: good. plan: 1) keep prefetch disabled for rollout group until we patch keying tests; 2) revert the tokenizer-normalize change in kernel and re-run e2e with cache keying test harness; 3) add a diagnostic that records hash input before/after normalization to catch regressions; 4) post-incident follow-up with owner of kernel perf PR.

mike: creating a GH issue now and tagging the kernel PR for revert + tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/2418

emma: incident mitigation checklist: prefetch disabled, nodes scaled, kernel flag reverted, ops rate-limit applied. rolling to monitoring until hit-rate > 80% for 10m.

dave: thumbs up. please also add a synthetic warmup job to the canary pipeline that simulates hot prefixes and validates hit-rate before traffic ramp.

sara: agreed. action items assigned: @mike revert + tests, @chris add diagnostics, @emma add autoscaler hook and warmup job, @dave write canary warmup job. I’ll write the incident summary.

mike: quick note — we should also add an integration test that runs the new kernel with various unicode combos to ensure no unintended normalization differences.

chris: postmortem item: key versioning. maybe include a key-version byte in the cache key so normalization changes are explicit and avoid silent stampedes.

emma: recording metrics we’ll attach to postmortem: hit-rate timeline, origin qps, cache CPU, kernel rollout timestamps, sample mismatched keys.

sara: thanks team. keep this thread updated — if anyone sees residual 5xx or >100ms latency from the cache layer after 11:00 UTC call it out here. :thumbsup:

mike: noted — i'll follow up with the PR link and timeline in the morning.

chris: closing loop: all mitigations green at 10:48 UTC, hit-rate back to ~87% at 10:55. will reconvene in postmortem doc.
summary: Cache miss stampede after kernel-selection rollout caused key normalization drift; mitigated by disabling prefetch, scaling cache nodes, and reverting tokenizer normalization flag. Follow-ups: tests, diagnostics, and warmup jobs.
